This individual, the appellant, was also a chief promoter and later the Secretary of the MCH Society, which was established in 1964 to build residences for Bank employees and other members.

However, a government order dated November 29, 1969, nullified the Registrar's orders of April 23 and October 21, 1969, and mandated a new inquiry.

On December 17, 1969, the Bank issued a show cause notice to the appellant, demanding an explanation within fifteen days for his alleged negligence as detailed in the October 4, 1969 report. Meanwhile, the Registrar appointed P2 on July 26, 1969, to conduct inquiries under Section S of A1. The appellant replied on January 18/22, 1970, providing his explanation and contesting the inquiry's legality and findings.

On March 5, 1970, P3, the Society's treasurer and a Bank employee, filed criminal complaints with the Addl. Chief Presidency Magistrate, accusing the appellant and two others of criminal breach of trust for dishonestly misappropriating Rs. 51,000/- and Rs. 80,000/- entrusted to the appellant as Promoter and Secretary. The Magistrate framed charges. The Bank suspended the appellant on November 3, 1970, pending trial, citing serious misconduct involving moral turpitude. The appellant protested, claiming he was not heard before the suspension.

P2, the authorized officer, in an order dated October 9, 1971, held the appellant liable for Rs. 2,36,000/- to the Society, in addition to Rs. 2,03,000/- for which he and two others were held jointly liable. Citing this finding, the Bank terminated the appellant's services with notice pay, effective December 1, 1971, via an order dated November 29, 1971. The appellant protested and filed a detailed representation on December 3, 1971. The Bank justified its action. On December 28, 1971, the appellant replied, arguing the termination was not simplicitor, violated natural justice principles as he was not heard, and attached a stigma.

The appellant appealed P2's findings to the Tribunal. The criminal proceedings resulted in a conviction by the Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate on March 27, 1972. The appellant appealed his conviction to the High Court. While that appeal was pending, the Tribunal dismissed the appellant's appeal on April 12, 1973, but reduced his liability by Rs. 72,000/-. A learned Single Judge granted the relief on December 6/7, 1979. The Bank appealed under Clause 15 of the Letters Patent. A Division Bench, in its judgment on April 16, 1985, allowed the appeal and dismissed the writ petition on grounds of laches and on merits. This appeal impugns the Division Bench's judgment and order.
